claims.quote: Patients have CACNA1A gene mutations resulting in truncation or single amino acid changes in the pore-forming subunit of Ca(v)2.1 (P/Q-type) Ca(2+) channels.
These neuronal channels mediate synaptic neurotransmitter release.
EA2 symptoms are thought to result from disturbed neurotransmission at cerebellar and neuromuscular synapses, caused by loss-of-function of Ca(v)2.1 channels.

claims.quote: EA2 symptoms are thought to result from disturbed neurotransmission at cerebellar and neuromuscular synapses, caused by loss-of-function of Ca(v)2.1 channels.
EA2 is treated with acetazolamide (AZA), but the pharmacotherapeutic mechanism is unknown.
Furthermore, AZA does not exert an acute, direct influence on the function of presynaptic (mutant) Ca(v)2.1 channels.

Our results indicate that Ln-mutated Ca(v)2.1 channels at Ln/wt NMJs are either normally inserted in the presynaptic membrane but have reduced function, or that they inhibit wild-type channels by hampering their expression, trafficking, membrane insertion and/or function.
